items.title: Eleven search hits not ingested
items.whyItMatters: The search reported 19 hits and returned 8; the rest are unappraised, so the review is incomplete until they are retrieved.
items.opportunity: Retrieve the remaining hits before screening closes and report the retrieval as a separate event.

items.title: Adherence measures disagree
items.whyItMatters: Refill data and self-report overstate adherence against electronic caps (claim c2).
items.opportunity: Tabulate adherence by measurement method; never combine methods.

items.title: Dose intensity is rarely reported as a harm
items.whyItMatters: Fewer severe toxicities may come with less treatment (claim c4).
items.opportunity: Record relative dose intensity as a balancing outcome wherever reported.

items.title: Highest-risk patients are least studied
items.whyItMatters: Patients over 75, living alone, far from the centre or needing interpreters carry most admissions (claim c7) but are rarely included.
items.opportunity: Chart the age, living situation, distance and language of every study population and state who is not covered.

items.title: Costs rest on one before-after budget analysis
items.whyItMatters: The saving range overlaps the cost (claim c5) and is not adjusted for case mix.
items.opportunity: Report costs as ranges with their assumptions, separately from effects.

errorsFound: A single summary figure combining adherence gains with cost savings would repeat the committee's earlier problem; the strands must stay separate.
reevaluation: The gaps confirm a narrowed rapid review with strands reported separately, adherence by method, dose intensity as a balancing outcome and an explicit statement of who is not covered.
summary: Five gaps: incomplete retrieval, disagreeing measures, dose intensity, equity and thin cost evidence.
